category_description: Social Security and Medicare benefits and the rules for claiming them in the United States.
subcategory_description: Medicare premiums, deductibles and how they change.
label: Standard Medicare Part B monthly premium
context: Paid by most Part B enrollees. Higher-income beneficiaries pay an income-related monthly adjustment on top.

label: Medicare Part B annual deductible
context: The annual deductible for all Part B beneficiaries.

label: Medicare Part A inpatient hospital deductible
context: What a beneficiary pays if admitted to the hospital. It covers the first 60 days of Medicare-covered inpatient hospital care in a benefit period.

label: Part A monthly premium with 30 to 39 quarters of coverage
context: For people who had at least 30 quarters of coverage, or were married to someone who did, and who buy into Part A at a reduced rate.

label: Part A monthly premium with fewer than 30 quarters of coverage
context: The full premium for certain uninsured aged individuals with fewer than 30 quarters of coverage, and certain people with disabilities who have exhausted other entitlements.

label: Income above which the Part B premium rises, individual returns
context: Modified adjusted gross income above this amount on an individual tax return brings an income-related monthly adjustment.

label: Income above which the Part B premium rises, joint returns
context: Modified adjusted gross income above this amount on a joint tax return brings an income-related monthly adjustment.

subject_intro: The standard Medicare Part B premium and deductible, how higher incomes pay more, and the Part A premium and hospital deductible.
